title: Guaranteed capacity obligations and degradation remediation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define legally-consumable SLA wording, measurement methodology, error budget accounting, and operational remediation playbooks for Dedicated capacity customers. This ticket captures proposed contract language, the engineering measurements required, the interplay with autoscaling/fleet controls, and an actionable runbook for when guarantees are degraded.
acceptance_criteria: Contract clause draft that legal signs off on for use in Dedicated offers
Measurement spec for throughput and availability with telemetry implementation plan
Error budget and credit calculator documented and validated with demo numbers
Operations remediation playbook that maps states (degraded, breached, recovery) to actions and timelines
Hand-off to Sales/CS with FAQ and negotiation levers list
proposed_sla_text: Redwood Inference guarantees a baseline committed throughput (CT) measured in megatokens-per-minute (MTPM) per customer region for each Dedicated deployment. CT will be specified in the Order Form. Measurement window: 5-minute rolling windows with 99th-percentile token completion rate computed daily. An incident is recorded when the measured 99th-percentile throughput for a customer region falls below 95% of CT for three consecutive 5-minute windows, excluding scheduled maintenance and pre-declared capacity reconfigurations. Error budget: Customer Error Budget (CEB) = CT * 24 * 60 * 30 * 0.05 (i.e., 5% tolerable degradation per month). If the accumulated minutes of degradation exceed the CEB within a billing month, Redwood will provide service credits equal to 10% of the monthly dedicated capacity fee prorated to the exceeded portion, unless controlled by force majeure. Remedies: Upon breach Redwood will (1) notify customer within 60 minutes, (2) execute immediate mitigation (scale-to-reserve and traffic-reroute), (3) provide root-cause analysis within 72 hours, and (4) apply credits per the above schedule. Termination rights apply only after three independent monthly breaches in a 12-month period with 30-day cure period for Redwood to remediate.
measurement_methodology: Throughput is derived from normalized token-completion counts emitted by runtime telemetry. Key measurements: 5-minute rolling window token throughput, 99th-percentile request completion time, queue depth, and per-model KV-cache hit rate. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows posted >= 48 hours, customer-initiated load tests flagged via support ticket, and pre-authorized model changes. Data sources: runtime /metrics endpoint (prometheus-style), per-tenant request logs, and regional load-balancer counters. The canonical measurement job lives in infra-metrics and computes daily aggregates retained for 13 months.
error_budget_policy: Accumulation: minutes of 5-minute windows below 95% of CT accumulate against the monthly CEB
Alerting: when 50% of CEB consumed -> notify SRE/CS and begin mitigation playbook
Depletion: when CEB exhausted -> escalate to on-call SRE and enable automatic burst on reserved pool up to burst-cap configured, and begin applying credits if recovery exceeds 60 minutes
Post-breach: full RCA within 72 hours, remediation milestones, and a 1:1 follow-up meeting with customer if customer requests
Credits: computed per prorated exceed amount; legal to approve non-monetary remediation alternatives (engineering credits, priority migration assistance) per contract negotiation
autoscaling_interplay: Contract guarantees assume a minimum reserved pool (MRP) backing the customer’s CT. Autoscaling policies must honor a floor: the autoscaler may use burst capacity only if (a) MRP is saturated AND (b) current usage < CT + burst_threshold. Burst usage is billable at an elevated rate and does not count toward reducing CEB. Scaling cooldowns are set to 60s for upscales and 300s for downscales to avoid oscillation. When a customer requests higher CT during a term, a provisioning lead time of 72 hours applies for capacity commitment; immediate increases are possible subject to global capacity availability and may be marked as provisional (best-effort) until formal allocation completes.
fleet_controls: regional_pinning: ability to pin a Dedicated fleet to specific AZs/regions to preserve latency and regulatory guarantees
drain_mode: deterministic drain with soft-stop window to finish in-flight KV-cache sequences before node recycle
circuit_breaker_thresholds: per-tenant request-rate thresholds that trigger traffic shedding with exponential backoff
canary_sequencing: staged rollout lanes that ensure at least one warm replica set per region before traffic switchover
capacity_reservation_tags: contract-linked tags to prevent autoscaler from rebalancing reserved nodes during scale events
